findings.title: canManage() is granted to callers who only have VIEW on all groups
findings.body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` evaluates `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`. Because any matching scope grants access, an admin with only an all-groups VIEW permission passes `requireManage()`. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` relies on that check, so a view-only admin can create top-level groups or move existing groups to the top level. This is a privilege escalation. Only `MANAGE` should be accepted here. The interface javadoc for `canManage()` repeats the same error ("VIEW or MANAGE") and should also be corrected.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs and misses per-group resources
findings.body:
There are three problems in this method.

1. Per-group resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` never get a type set. Only the schema's all-groups resource has type "Groups", so `findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` will not return per-group resources.
2. The callback passes `groupResource.getId()` (the authz resource id) into `hasPermission`. That method treats the value as a group id and calls `findByName`, so the lookup always falls back to the all-groups resource.
3. The callback adds `groupResource.getId()` to the result set. Group resources are named by group id, so the set holds resource ids rather than group ids.

Callers use this set as group ids: `UserModel.GROUPS` for user search and `getUsersCount(..., groupIds)`. As a result, user counts for group-scoped admins are wrong, and user search filtering by group either matches nothing or matches incorrectly. The new tests only pass because per-user `canView` filtering is applied afterwards on an unfiltered stream, which also breaks pagination. The method should use `resource.getName()` (the group id) and find per-group resources by a means that does not depend on their type.

findings.title: V1 group-removal listener now hits UnsupportedOperationException under V2
findings.body:
Before this change, `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` was inherited and returned the V1 `GroupPermissions`. It now returns `GroupPermissionsV2`, whose `setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`.

`AdminPermissions.registerListener` (active when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled) calls `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)` on every `GroupRemovedEvent`. When V2 is also enabled, `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2`. In that configuration, deleting any group would fail with a 500.

V2 management should either no-op here or the listener should skip V2.

findings.title: requireManageMembers javadoc references the wrong method
findings.body: The javadoc for `requireManageMembers` says it throws if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false. The implementations actually check `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`. Readers will be misled about which permission is enforced.
